checkpoints.description: [1/4] Pre-register ADR-013 and add failing tests for the Gaussian Madelung reduction

impact_assessment.why: The Madelung dictionary and Nelson kinematics are exact, but the quantum ground-state width was still inserted. A Gaussian ansatz reduces the fluid equations to the Ermakov equation; its fixed point should be the quantum width hbar/(2m omega).
impact_assessment.benefits: A self-consistent fluid derivation of the ground-state width without using the Schrodinger solution, plus a numerical test of the fixed point and its oscillation frequency.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new claim 22, no existing claim changes; dependency: numpy only; concurrency: none; state: one result file; numerical: RK4 step and energy conservation
impact_assessment.mitigation: Derive the effective potential analytically; pre-register the fixed-point identity, the 2 omega oscillation frequency, and an energy-drift tolerance; integrate with RK4 at dt=1e-3

[1/4] Pre-register ADR-014 and add failing tests for the moving-center Gaussian reduction

impact_assessment.why: The ground-state Gaussian reduction derived the width but held the center fixed. A displaced Gaussian tests whether the fluid equations separate into classical center motion and the quantum width, and covers the coherent state without the node singularity of the first excited state.
impact_assessment.benefits: A second self-consistent derivation: the center follows x0''=-omega^2 x0 and the width keeps the Ermakov fixed point, with a numerical check of the trajectory and energy.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new claim 23, no existing claim changes; dependency: numpy only; concurrency: none; state: one result file; numerical: coupled RK4 and energy conservation
impact_assessment.mitigation: Derive the center and width equations analytically; pre-register the 2 pi period, the fixed-point width, and an energy-drift tolerance; integrate with RK4 at dt=1e-3

[1/4] Pre-register ADR-015 and add failing tests for the first-excited-state node

impact_assessment.why: The Gaussian reductions cover node-free states. The first excited state has a density node at x=0, where the Madelung phase and quantum pressure may be singular; this must be tested before the fluid program can claim excited states.
impact_assessment.benefits: Identifies the exact limit of the single-valued fluid representation and motivates a two-component or defect model; also verifies the regular quantum pressure away from the node.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new claim 24, no existing claim changes; dependency: numpy only; concurrency: none; state: one result file; numerical: the phase gradient is a central difference, so the discrete maximum is pi/(2dx) not pi/dx
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use the exact first-excited density and wavefunction; scan N=256,512,1024,2048; fit the log-log slope of the phase-gradient maximum; compare the regular Q at x=1 to the analytic expression

[1/4] Pre-register ADR-016 and add failing tests for the hydrogen 1s Madelung reduction

impact_assessment.why: The first excited state exposes the node singularity. The hydrogen 1s state is nodeless and realistic; its Coulomb attraction and quantum pressure should balance at the Bohr radius, testing the fluid program on a real quantum scale.
impact_assessment.benefits: A positive derivation of the Bohr radius and ground-state energy from the Madelung force balance, not from the Schrodinger wavefunction, extending the fluid program beyond Gaussian models.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new claim 25, no existing claim changes; dependency: numpy only; concurrency: none; state: one result file; numerical: the 1/r quantum pressure and the SI/atomic-unit conversion
impact_assessment.mitigation: Derive the 1/r coefficient and constant analytically; test the density normalization and the force-balance residual at several radii; report both atomic units and SI values

[1/4] Pre-register ADR-017 and add failing tests for the hydrogen 2p vortex identification

impact_assessment.why: The first excited state node is singular in 1D. The hydrogen 2p_(m=+-1) state has an angular node at the origin, which is a quantized vortex with circulation h/m_e, not a radial node. Identifying it connects the node problem to the earlier vortex work.
impact_assessment.benefits: A positive fluid-mechanics identification of a real quantum state: circulation, angular momentum and most-probable radius from the exact 2p density.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new claim 26, no existing claim changes; dependency: numpy only; concurrency: none; state: one result file; numerical: the azimuthal velocity diverges at theta=0, so the loop is evaluated away from the poles
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use the exact 2p radial function; test normalization, the 4a0 peak, the loop circulation away from the poles, and the angular momentum; state that m=0 has no vortex
